Τῑθωνός , ὁ, Tithonus, brother of Priam, husband of Eos, and father of Memnon, Il. 11.1 , 20.237 , Hes. Th. 984 . etc.: metaph. of a decrepit old man, because, as the tale went, Eos begged Zeus to grant immortality to Tithonus, but forgot to ask for eternal youth, Ar. Ach. 688 , Call. Iamb. 1.249 : prov. of great old age,
A. “ὑπὲρ τὸν Τ. ζῆν”
Luc. DMort. 7.1
.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
